root_cause.text: The driver wx_sw_init() unconditionally reads the PF-restricted register WX_CFG_PORT_ST to determine the bus function ID, even when the device is a VF, causing an illegal register access that hangs the system.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check `if (pdev->is_virtfn)` to avoid reading the PF-only register for VF devices, instead using PCI_FUNC(pdev->devfn).

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: The driver wx_sw_init() unconditionally reads the PF-restricted register WX_CFG_PORT_ST to determine the bus function ID, even when the device is a VF, causing an illegal register access that hangs the system.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds a check `if (pdev->is_virtfn)` to avoid reading the PF-only register for VF devices, instead using PCI_FUNC(pdev->devfn).

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix bus function retrieval for virtual functions by using PCI_FUNC instead of hardware register read.
intent_record.what: Replaced unconditional assignment of wx->bus.func with a conditional: if the device is a virtual function (pdev->is_virtfn), use PCI_FUNC(pdev->devfn); otherwise use the original FIELD_GET(WX_CFG_PORT_ST_LANID, rd32(wx, WX_CFG_PORT_ST)).
intent_record.how: For physical functions, behavior remains the same. For virtual functions, wx->bus.func is now correctly derived from the PCI device function number instead of reading a hardware register that may not be valid for VFs, preventing incorrect function identification.

grouping_result.intent: Fix bus function retrieval for virtual functions by using PCI_FUNC instead of hardware register read.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly fixes the root cause by replacing the unconditional hardware register read with PCI_FUNC for virtual functions, preventing illegal register access on VFs.
